paper_metadata.title: Altered Microstructural Changes Detected by Diffusion Kurtosis Imaging in Patients With Cognitive Impairment After Acute Cerebral Infarction

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the target population, recruitment setting (tertiary hospital), and specific inclusion/exclusion criteria. A sample size calculation was performed, and baseline characteristics were comparable across groups, minimizing selection bias.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: A total of 70 patients with acute cerebral infarction were enrolled in this study in a tertiary hospital, including 35 patients with cognitive impairment (VCI group, the mean age was 66.3 years, 17 males and 18 females), and 35 patients without cognitive impairment (N-VCI group, the mean age was 63.1 years, 15 males and 20 females).
items.reasoning: The authors clearly define the source (tertiary hospital) and provide demographic details for the groups.

items.reasoning: The recruitment of both patients and healthy controls is described, and a sample size calculation was used to ensure adequacy.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factor (DKI parameters) is measured using a standardized 3.0T MRI protocol. The use of two experienced radiologists and blinding of technicians further reduces measurement bias.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: DKI parameters include both diffusion parameters [fractional anisotropy (FA), mean diffusion (MD), axial diffusion (Da), and radial diffusion (Dr)] and kurtosis parameters [fractional anisotropy kurtosis (FAK), mean kurtosis (MK), axial kurtosis (Ka) and radial kurtosis (Kr)]
items.reasoning: The parameters are explicitly defined and the mathematical basis (cumulant expansion) is provided.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: Two radiologists (YD and CY, with 10 years and 17 years of experience in neuroimaging, respectively), assessed the images, drew ROIs and checked them.
items.reasoning: The use of two experienced radiologists and a consensus model for ROI drawing ensures reliability.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: at the optimal cut-off MD value (0.9915), sensitivity was 91.4%, specificity 100%
items.reasoning: While continuous data are used for correlations, the ROC analysis uses an 'optimal' cut-off which is by definition data-dependent.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: All subjects underwent DKI scans within 4-7 days of admission... using a GE MR750W 3.0T magnetic resonance scanner.
items.reasoning: Standardized equipment and timing were used for all participants.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (cognitive impairment) was measured using the MMSE, a validated and widely used clinical tool. The evaluators were professionally trained, and the criteria for impairment were pre-specified.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: MMSE scores were used to evaluate overall cognitive function, where an MMSE score < 27 was considered objective cognitive impairment
items.reasoning: The outcome is clearly defined using a validated scale and a specific cut-off score.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: All subjects were assessed by two professionally trained neuropsychological evaluators using a neuropsychological scale during the visit.
items.reasoning: The use of trained evaluators and a validated scale (MMSE) supports reliability.

items.evidence_snippet: All subjects were assessed by two professionally trained neuropsychological evaluators using a neuropsychological scale during the visit.
items.reasoning: The protocol was applied consistently to all groups.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical methods are generally appropriate for the data type, but the reliance on Pearson correlations and the lack of multivariable adjustment (e.g., linear regression) limits the strength of the prognostic conclusions. The ROC analysis is well-reported.
